name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

areaKm2.note: World Bank land area 241,930 km2; total area incl. inland water ~242,500 km2 (mid); polygon world_1960 United Kingdom computes to ~219,000 km2 on the sphere (coarse coastline), so the polygon is not used.

population.note: OWID population 1989 = 57,182,137 (mid); World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 1989 = 57,076,711 (low); COW NMC v7 tpop 1989 = 57,358k (high). UK only, excludes Crown dependencies and overseas territories.

urbanization.note: OWID/HYDE urban share UK 1989 = 88.7%. Low allows for narrower urban definitions.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: ACTIVE 311,650 incl 16,250 women and some 9,200 enlisted outside the UK (Army 155,500, RN incl. Marines 64,650, RAF 91,450). COW NMC v7 milper 1989 = 318k (high). Options for Change (July 1990) cut ~18% to ~255,000 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Options_for_Change, citing Hansard 25 July 1990). Excludes the Royal Ulster Constabulary.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: RESERVES 325,000 (Army 255,200 incl. regular reserve 173,100, TA 72,800, HSF ~3,000, UDR 6,300; Navy 30,300; Marines 3,700; RAF 35,700). Low excludes the ~25,000 Royal Fleet Reserve ex-regulars with no training commitment and part of the regular army reserve.

supportPersonnel.note: Everything outside the infantry P roles: RN (64,650 incl. Marines but less the 3 commando infantry) and RAF (91,450) entirely, plus Army armour, artillery, engineers, signals, aviation, logistics and staffs. = active 311,650 minus ~41,000 infantry (reconstruction from the MB 1989-90 order of battle).

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogue: united-kingdom-1939 snapshot (WWII peak ~5.1M in uniform of ~48M = 0.106, Harrison 1998). Scaled down for 1989: no conscription law since 1960, long-service volunteer force, equipment stocks for a short war only.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: 20 mech inf bn (10 FV 432, 10 Saxon) and 3 armd inf bn (Warrior) = 23 bn at ~600-700 riflemen and support each. Reconstruction from the order of battle; MB gives no personnel by arm.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: SA80 rifle entering service, Milan ATGW, Warrior IFV only in 3 bn; 10 bn still on 1960s FV 432 and 10 on wheeled Saxon

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: long-service volunteers, BATUS Suffield and Soltau exercises, Northern Ireland tours

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: 29 inf bn (incl 5 Gurkha) + 3 AB bn + 1 SAS regt + 3 RM commandos (RM 7,700 total). ~35 units at ~600-750 each. Reconstruction from the order of battle; Territorial Army 41 inf bn are trainedReserves.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: light role battalions with Milan, 81 mm mortars, Rapier/Javelin support; limited protected mobility

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Parachute Regiment, Gurkhas, Royal Marines and SAS elite long-service units; Falklands combat veterans in the NCO corps

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: towed 229 (150 L-118 105 mm, 79 FH-70) + SP 321 (159 Abbot, 110 M-109, 36 M-107, 16 M-110) + 4 MLRS (trials) = 554 tubes/launchers. Mortars (~500 81 mm) excluded; Lance counted under missiles.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: M-109/FH-70 era-typical; MLRS arriving; Abbot obsolescent

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: Royal Artillery professional, BATUS live-fire; Falklands experience

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: MBT 1,290 = ~420 Challenger + 870 Chieftain incl 400 in store; light tanks 271 FV 101 Scorpion (+36 Scorpion with the RAF Regiment). Mid = 890 active MBT + 271 Scorpion; low = active MBT only; high = all MBT incl store + all Scorpion.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Challenger 1 with Chobham armour; Chieftain with 120 mm rifled gun but weak engine; store tanks older

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional crews, BAOR gunnery camps; Challenger fire control weaker than Leopard 2 (Canadian Army Trophy 1987 last place)

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: AIFV ~200 Warrior; APC 3,437 (2,338 FV 432 incl variants, ~60 Saracen, 12 Saladin, 500 Spartan, ~527 Saxon). High adds 990 recce vehicles (290 Scimitar, 500 Ferret, ~200 Fox) and 90 RAF Regiment Spartan.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: mostly 1960s FV 432; Warrior modern but only ~200 delivered

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional mechanised infantry

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: RAF Phantom 90 (18 FG-1, 12 F-3 ex F-4J, 60 FGR-2) + Tornado F-2/F-3 66 (48 ftr, 18 OCU) + FAA Sea Harrier FRS-1 42 = 198. Low excludes OCU; high adds 59 Tornado F-2/F-3 in store and 72 Sidewinder-capable Hawks of the tactical weapons units.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Tornado F-3 with Foxhunter radar and Sky Flash, but Phantoms ageing; no F-15/Su-27 class fighter

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: NATO TACEVAL, Red Flag participation; Sea Harrier pilots with Falklands combat record

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: Tornado GR-1 161 (108 strike, 12 recce, 20 TTTE, 21 weapons conversion) + Buccaneer 34 + Jaguar 87 + Harrier 51 = 333. Low = front-line only (108+12+25+72+36 = 253); high adds 149 in store (51 GR-1, 25 Buccaneer, 55 Jaguar, 18 Harrier). Nimrod MR-2 (34) excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Tornado GR-1 terrain-following all-weather strike with JP233 and WE.177; Harrier GR-5 entering service

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: intensive low-level training, Red Flag, Tornado TTTE

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: Army 313 (30 Scout, 159 SA-341 Gazelle, 120 Lynx some with TOW, 4 A-109); RN 220 (120 Sea King, 78 Lynx, 22 Gazelle trg); RM 14; RAF 168 (64 Wessex, 32 CH-47, 31 Puma, 19 Sea King SAR, 22 Gazelle). Low excludes training and SAR airframes.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Lynx/TOW and Sea King capable; no dedicated attack helicopter (Apache only from 2001)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional Army Air Corps and FAA

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: principal surface combatants 49 = 2 Invincible CVS (plus 1 in store, high) + 13 DDG (12 Type 42, 1 Bristol) + 34 frigates (3 Type 22 B3, 10 Type 22, 6 Type 21, 15 Leander). Low excludes 8 in refit. LPDs counted as minor (project convention, see usa-2026).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Sea Wolf point defence and Type 22/23 ASW world-class; small carriers with 8 Sea Harriers, no AEW aircraft (Sea King AEW only)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Flag Officer Sea Training work-ups; 1982 combat lessons; Armilla patrol in the Gulf 1987-88

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: patrol and coastal combatants 44 + mine countermeasures 38 + amphibious 7 (2 Fearless LPD, 5 RFA LSL) = 89. Low excludes RNR-manned MCM.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Hunt-class GRP MCMV among the best; patrol craft basic

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional RN; some MCM manned by RNR

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: 31 = 4 Resolution SSBN (Polaris A-3TK) + 16 SSN (5 Trafalgar, 6 Swiftsure, 2 Valiant, 3 Churchill) + 11 Oberon SS; 5 in refit (low).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Trafalgar/Swiftsure SSN among the quietest NATO boats; Spearfish not yet in service

training.note: Rubric row: training 1.0. Evidence: Perisher command course; continuous deterrent patrols; Cold War under-ice and trailing operations

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: SSM 14 Lance launchers incl 2 in store (1 SSM regt with 12 launchers). The 64 Polaris SLBM tubes are carried by the SSBN counted under submarines (project convention, see usa-2026).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Lance 1970s nuclear/conventional SSM, 120 km range

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional Royal Artillery missile regiment

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), UK entry, as transcribed at the cited page: Army 3 Rapier regt with 120 Rapier fire units (~9-10 batteries of 12); RAF Regiment 6 Rapier SAM sqn (72 launchers); RAF 2 Bloodhound 2 sqn (64 launchers, ~4 flights); RAuxAF 1 Oerlikon/Skyguard sqn. ~22 battery-equivalents. TA Blowpipe/Javelin MANPADS regiments excluded. Battery count is a conversion, grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Rapier (Blindfire) effective low-level SAM; no long-range Patriot-class system, Bloodhound 1960s

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional; Rapier combat use in 1982

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75. Evidence: trained joint staff system, 1982 Falklands success; Bagnall reforms of 1 (BR) Corps operational doctrine (counter-stroke) 1983-87

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75-1.0. Evidence: regimental system with strong unit identity; all-volunteer force

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: peacetime force, confident after 1982; Northern Ireland strain; overstretch and retention problems

weapons.note: Anchor: 9 (1985: guided missiles, MBTs with FCS, jets). Evidence: Challenger, Tornado with JP233/ALARM, Sea Wolf, Milan, MLRS trials; much legacy kit (Chieftain, FV 432, Abbot)

armor.note: Anchor: 9 (composite armour). Evidence: ~420 Challenger with Chobham composite armour (UK invention), but 870 Chieftain with cast steel

ships.note: Anchor: 9 (nuclear subs, Aegis). Evidence: 16 SSN, Polaris SSBN, Sea Dart/Sea Wolf; no Aegis-class area defence, small carriers

fortification.note: Anchor: 9 (hardened shelters). Evidence: hardened aircraft shelters at RAF Germany bases, NATO hardened command posts

logistics.note: Anchor: 9 (containerised, airlift). Evidence: VC-10/TriStar strategic airlift and tankers, RFA fleet; 1982 showed reliance on requisitioned merchant ships

communications.note: Anchor: 9 (satellite comms, data links). Evidence: Skynet 4A launched 1990, Skynet 2 earlier; Ptarmigan trunk system in BAOR (1985); Link 11/16 at sea

isr.note: Anchor: 9 (satellites). Evidence: Nimrod R-1 ELINT, Tornado GR-1A recce, GCHQ; access to US satellite imagery; AEW still on Shackleton (E-3D Sentry from 1991)

air.note: Anchor: air 9 = 1985. Evidence: Tornado GR-1/F-3, Harrier GR-5 entering service; Phantoms ageing; no look-down shoot-down fighter beyond Tornado F-3

cyber.note: Anchor: cyber 9 = 1990 networks. Evidence: GCHQ SIGINT and computer centres, MoD networks; no offensive network capability documented in 1989

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV): United Kingdom 1989 = 26,164 (2011 int$).

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS: 1989 = 4.04%, 1988 = 4.21% (high), 1990 = 3.98% (low). Peacetime.

industrialShare.note: World Bank industry incl. construction value added: 1990 = 27.6%, 1991 = 26.9% (series starts 1990). 1989 slightly higher; high allows for North Sea oil in industry.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) United Kingdom 1989 = 2.2%. The UK was a net food importer; that does not lower this value. Share 2.2% (range 1.5-3.5%) -> 0.978 (0.965-0.985).

annualCohort.note: World Bank SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y GBR 1989 = 7.52% of males aged 15-19; applied to total population 57.1M (female share assumed equal) / 5 = ~859,000 persons per year (~430,000 males).

artillery.note: Educated guess: towed L-118 light guns and FH-70; AS-90 not yet in production.

armor.note: Educated guess: wartime tank output per year: Challenger built at Vickers Leeds and ROF; Challenger 2 programme pending; surge limited by a single production line.

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess: Warrior (GKN Telford) ~200-300 per year plus Saxon wheeled APC.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess: Tornado F-3 at BAe Warton, UK share of the trinational line.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess: Tornado GR-1 (UK share) plus Harrier GR-5/7 at Kingston/Dunsfold.

helicopters.note: Educated guess: Westland Lynx/Sea King/EH-101 line at Yeovil.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: Type 23 frigates (Yarrow, Swan Hunter) about 2-3 a year in 1989-92; carrier surge not possible.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess: Sandown/Hunt MCMV and patrol craft.

submarines.note: Educated guess: VSEL Barrow: Trafalgar SSN, Vanguard SSBN and Upholder SSK building in parallel.

air_defense.note: Educated guess: Rapier fire units by BAe Dynamics, in battery equivalents.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: public road network of Great Britain ~350,000 km plus Northern Ireland ~24,000 km, all paved.

railKm.note: World Bank rail lines 1995 = 17,001 km (first value in the series); British Rail route length ~16,600 km in 1989 plus NIR ~330 km. Grade C (series starts after the snapshot).

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: London/Tilbury, Felixstowe, Southampton, Portsmouth, Plymouth, Liverpool, Glasgow/Clyde, Rosyth/Forth, Belfast, Hull, Tees, Bristol.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: UK-registered merchant fleet fell from ~30M grt (1975) to roughly 5-7M grt by 1989 after flagging out; x1.5 to dwt. Plus a large UK-owned foreign-flag fleet that could be requisitioned (STUFT, as in 1982).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: BAOR planned a forward defence with corps depots 100-300 km behind the IGB; out-of-area reach shown in 1982 (12,800 km by sea via Ascension) but land radius from a beachhead was ~100 km.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses and ponies in the UK (riding and leisure), no military transport role.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS (Kristensen and Korda) via OWID: United Kingdom 1989 = 350 warheads. Polaris A-3TK Chevaline (64 msl x 2 RV) plus WE.177 free-fall bombs for Tornado/Buccaneer/Sea Harrier and RN ASW depth bombs. US-custody Lance/artillery warheads for BAOR not counted.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: island with sea moat, familiar terrain, population support; no strategic depth or harsh climate. BAOR fights forward in the FRG at 1.0.

notes: Snapshot date mid-1989 (IISS Military Balance 1989-1990, data as at 1 June 1989), before the fall of the Berlin Wall and Options for Change (1990). Population convention: UK only (OWID); Hong Kong, Gibraltar, Falklands and other dependencies excluded, their garrisons listed as basesAbroad. Personnel: active = regular forces 311,650; TA, regular reserve, UDR and RN/RAF reserves = trainedReserves. Infantry P roles are reconstructed from battalion counts; everything else is supportPersonnel. Deployed abroad (MB 1989-90): FRG 69,700 (BAOR 55,700, Berlin 3,000, RAF Germany 11,000), Cyprus 3,900, Hong Kong 8,200, Falklands ~1,600, Belize 1,500, Gibraltar 1,800, Brunei ~900, so not all forces are at home on day one. The MB edition was read from a full-text transcription at samlib.ru (cited URL); the printed volume is Brassey's for IISS, 1989. Equipment in store is in high only. Weakest values: merchant tonnage, road length and wartime production rates (educated guesses).
